title: Smart 3V board setup
lead: Install Smart 3V on a new board over USB and get its pairing code. After that, updates arrive through Home Assistant.
unsupported: This browser can't talk to USB devices. Open this page in Chrome or Edge on a computer.

connect.title: Plug it in
connect.cable: Connect the board to this computer with a USB cable that carries data, not a charge-only cable. Close any other program that is talking to it.
connect.boot: Won't connect? Unplug it, hold the BOOT button, plug it back in, then let go.
erase.warning: Installing erases the board. A board that was already paired loses that pairing and gets a new code.

next.title: After setup: add the board and keep it up to date
next.intro: Do steps 2 and 3 once for each Home Assistant. After that, every board you add gets updates automatically.
next.add.title: Add the board to Home Assistant
next.add.text: Go to Settings, Devices & services, Add device, then Add Matter device. Scan the QR code or type the 11-digit number. Keep your phone near the board and make sure your Thread border router is on.
next.addon.title: Install the Smart 3V Updater add-on
next.addon.text: It watches for new Smart 3V versions and offers them in Home Assistant. Newer Home Assistant versions call add-ons apps.
next.addon.button: Add the add-on to my Home Assistant
next.addon.manual: Or add this address yourself under Settings, Add-ons (Apps), Add-on store, the ⋮ menu, Repositories:
next.dcl.title: Turn on test devices in the Matter Server
next.dcl.text: Open the Matter Server add-on, go to Configuration, turn on enable_test_net_dcl, save, and restart it. Smart 3V boards are prototypes and need this setting to receive updates.
next.install.title: Install updates when they appear
next.install.text: New versions show up under Settings, Updates. Click Update on each board. It takes about 5 to 6 minutes, and the board must stay powered the whole time.
next.limits.title: Not using Home Assistant OS?
next.limits.text: Add-ons need Home Assistant OS or a Supervised install. Home Assistant in Docker can control the boards but can't install the add-on, so it gets no automatic updates.
next.other.title: Using Apple Home or Google Home?
next.other.text: Updates only arrive through Home Assistant with the add-on. Apple Home users can also add the board to a Home Assistant, because a Matter device can belong to both at once; Home Assistant then delivers the updates. Without Home Assistant, the only way to update is to install again over USB on this page, which erases the board so it has to be added again. Google Home doesn't accept these prototype boards.
